name: The 2022 Self-Audit
claim: In Congress 117 (2021-2022), Democratic members' press releases repeated the same five-word phrases from one week to the next at a higher rate than Republican members' -- matched weekly 5-gram overlap 0.00176 vs 0.00095 (~85% higher), with Democrats higher in 75 of 105 weeks (71%), a gap that widened rather than closed when co-signed releases were removed -- replicating OnScript's 2022 Twitter-era result on official press releases; the figure measures week-to-week textual overlap, not coordination or intent.

numbers.metric: mean pairwise weekly content-5-gram Jaccard overlap, member counts matched per party per week (min per party, cap 40)

joint_release_control.effect: excluding verbatim co-signed releases WIDENED the D>R gap; R co-signs more, so co-signing works against the finding

confounds_tested: member-count asymmetry -> controlled: parties subsampled to equal N per week (min per party, cap 40)
joint/co-signed releases -> controlled: verbatim cross-member releases excluded; gap WIDENED (D 0.00173->0.00176, R 0.00102->0.00095); R dropped more (48 vs 37), so co-signing is not the driver
coverage -> both parties measured in the same weeks; scale-free per-pair Jaccard removes corpus-volume/density sensitivity
split_result: n/a as a chronological split (pre-registered as a targeted replication of the 2021-2022 window, not a two-half test); internal robustness = Democrats higher in 71% of the 105 matched weeks
chart_spec: paired weekly overlap line, D vs R across the 105 weeks of 2021-2022 (shade the 75 weeks D>R); or two mean bars (0.00176 vs 0.00095) annotated '71% of weeks'
receipts_note: receipts = specific high-peak Democratic 5-grams in Congress 117 from the phrase index (a phrase carried by 30+ D members in one week), each expandable to member + date + URL; pull at publish time from the member-augmented index
republication_note: CONFIRMED in the pre-registered direction (2021-2022 replication of the 2022 predecessor finding) -- no re-pre-registration required; only reversal/descriptive candidates need re-pre-registration in the found direction before publishing, and this is not one
neutrality_gate: PARTY-ASYMMETRIC (D > R): before publish, apply the power-position reframe -- higher week-to-week phrase overlap is a measurable property of each party's press operation (message discipline), stated symmetrically, not a virtue or vice -- and pass neutrality review; flag that the related Democratic rise concentrates in the 2023-25 House-minority years (see S1.4), so the finding is not read as an intrinsic partisan trait
